item: 5-tier networked stack light, PoE (option a, RECOMMENDED), one per station
seller: Wolf Automation (Marshall Wolf Automation, Algonquin IL)
pack: 1 tower: 60 mm, 5 tiers of multi-colour LEDs, 85 dB buzzer (11 sounds), off-white body, direct mount, RJ-45 PoE
qty_basis: 14 stations: the 12 MiR250 docks (glovebox, rePowder atomizer, sieve cell, 2 Kardex Shuttle VLMs, Aconity, packaging, 2 Instrons, fume hood, DED cell, wire EDM) + the EOS M400 and Meltio cells; 1 tower each = 14. Less any machine whose own tower can be re-ordered (checked on site). Per station with the bracket: $684.90 + $28.56 = $713.46; x14 = $9,988.44.

alt.stock_or_lead_time: Availability: Factory stock (lead time by quote)

notes: Control, per Patlite's spec sheet (https://www.wolfautomation.com/content/patlite-lasix-poe-directmount.pdf): HTTP, Modbus/TCP and socket (Patlite's PNS/PHN commands), DHCP, web setup tool; SNMP is not listed. It also has 8 wired contact inputs (relay/NPN/PNP) plus a flash enable, so a machine's own PLC can drive it by wire. Each lamp can be steady or flashing at 30/60/120 per min (default 60). Power: PoE IEEE 802.3af Class 0, 8.6 W typical and 12.5 W max at 48 V, or 24 VDC on the terminal block. IP54, indoor, upright, -10 to +50 C. The tiers are multi-colour: signal-tower mode offers red, yellow, green, blue, white, purple, pink, lemon yellow and sky blue. Set them to R/Y/G/B/W from the top (use 'yellow', not 'lemon yellow'), lock the web settings, and check every tower on install, because the position cue (red on top) depends on a setting. Wolf's spec table says EtherNet/IP; Patlite's sheet does not, so trust the sheet. Wolf has 3 in stock, so the other 11 come from Patlite USA stock. Ask Wolf for a quote and lead time on 14. Allied lists about 4 weeks for the silver sibling (snippet; alliedelec.com returned 403). Wolf ships free on online orders over $350 and has tax-exempt steps. The silver-body LA6-5DTNUB-POE+FT015 is $719.10 at Wolf. Not included: one Cat5e-or-better cable from a PoE switch port to each tower. PoE switch ports needed: 14 x 802.3af. Class 0 makes the switch reserve 15.4 W a port, 216 W in all; the real draw is at most 175 W (12.5 W each) and typically about 120 W. 10/100 Mb/s is enough.

notes: Steady only ('permanent light function'), so the flashing has to come from the controller. That is fine with the CLICK PLC's solid-state outputs. Don't drive it from mechanical relays: flashing at 1 Hz is about 30,000 operations per 8-hour day. Check that the LS7's current per tier is within the CLICK's 0.1 A per output. Banner TL50/TL70 and Werma KombiSIGN 72 were not priced (time). AutomationDirect lists the Werma eSIGN instead, $442-$585.
